thread:
Maya: Quick brainstorm for the benchmark webinar narrative. We need a clean storyline: 1) Why tail latency ruins UX, 2) How cost per token hides throughput/latency tradeoffs, 3) Concrete levers teams can pull (quantize, batch, route). Looking for non-technical hooks for execs and 2 technical callouts for devs.

Jon: For exec hook: "Predictability beats peaks". For devs: show KV cache hit-rate impact and batching efficiency numbers.

Priya: Chart ideas: CDF of response times, bar chart of $/1k tokens per model+quant, and a simple decision flow for routing (edge vs reserved). Keep color palette on-brand.

Evan: I'll pull the last 14 days from analytics for redwood-1-medium and redwood-1-small. marketing-bot, can you generate baseline numbers for p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k tokens across models?

marketing-bot: fetched summary metrics for redwood-1-small & redwood-1-medium (14d). p50/p90/p99 and cost per 1k tokens attached.

Maya: Cool. Jon, can you draft the three social lines? Need variants for LinkedIn, X, and the webinar registration email subject.

Jon: Done: LinkedIn: "How latent tails shape customer trust: 30m webinar on making LLMs dependable without overspending." X: "Latency matters. Cost matters. Join us to see the tradeoffs." Email subject: "Webinar: Cut LLM inference costs while keeping latency predictable"

Priya: Routing CTA mapping (first pass): request shape -> suggest product funnel: low-concurrency inference with high latency sensitivity -> hosted w/ prefix caching; high-concurrency steady -> Dedicated reserved; mixed workloads -> hybrid with explicit policy routing.

Maya: Great. Evan, loop in product for a short demo script showing canary fallback in action. Also, need a 1-paragraph executive summary (2-3 sentences) for the registration page. Priya, can you mock that?

Priya: Exec summary draft: "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams deliver predictable inference at scale by combining a high-performance runtime with routing, caching, and cost-aware controls. In this webinar, well walk through real-world benchmarks that illustrate latency and cost tradeoffs, and share practical levers teams can use to cut costs while preserving user experience."

Maya: Nice. One more ask: capture 3 quick customer anecdotes (anonymized) about latency wins or cost reductions to use as microcase studies in the deck. Jon, Evan, split those 3.

Jon: will reach out to CS for 2 anonymized notes. Evan: you own the third.

Evan: on it. Will bring one with numbers by EOD.

Maya: thanks team. Let's reconvene 10am tomorrow to review the hero image and slide skeleton.
